verdict.summary: A General (OAuth) app works in your own Zoom account within minutes, but outside your account you either need Zoom's approval to share a beta app (capped at 10 account-level or 100 user-level installs, with URLs that expire after 4 weeks) or you must publish through Marketplace review, which includes a functional review and a security review with technical design documentation and OWASP testing. Zoom cites a 72-hour SLA per step and up to two weeks for security review, but developers report 6–8+ weeks.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create a General app, add redirect URL and scopes, install via Local Test in your own account.

timeToProd.assumes: A published Marketplace app (can be unlisted via 'install from your landing page') that reads meetings, recordings or transcripts for any Zoom user; a beta share to up to 100 external users takes 3–4 business days.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Marketplace functional review, then security review (technical design document review, scope evaluation, OWASP testing), plus any remediation rounds.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Zoom staff (Dec 2024) cite a 72-hour SLA per submission and up to 2 weeks for security review; forum reports through 2026 describe 6–8+ weeks. The official review page gives no timeframe.

verdict.cost: Free to build and submit; no review fee found. API rate limits depend on the customer's Zoom plan (Free accounts have low daily caps).

prerequisites.item: A Zoom account with permission to create Marketplace apps
prerequisites.why: Apps are created in the Marketplace developer console and tested by installing into your own account.

prerequisites.item: Public HTTPS redirect URL and an allow-list entry for it
prerequisites.why: The OAuth flow returns the code to your registered redirect URL.

prerequisites.item: For publishing: technical design documentation, security information, clear listing content, and a test plan
prerequisites.why: The submission completeness check and security review depend on them, and unclear scopes or listings lengthen review.

scopeTiers.impact: Private apps can be shared only with members of your own Zoom account; no review needed.
Request to Share needs Zoom approval; caps of 10 account-level / 100 user-level additions; URLs valid 4 weeks with two possible 4-week extensions. Fine for pilots, not production.

scopeTiers.tier: User-level scopes on a published app
scopeTiers.impact: Any Zoom user can install after Marketplace approval. Security review evaluates whether each scope is necessary.
Gives access across the whole account, so an account admin has to install it. Expect more scrutiny in scope evaluation.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Zoom's scope page lists :admin and :master variants but doesn't define them; reading them as account-admin / master-account access is our inference.

steps.title: Create a General (OAuth) app
steps.detail: Sign in to the App Marketplace, open the developer console and build a General app. Set the OAuth redirect URL, allow-list it, and add scopes.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: marketplace.zoom.us/develop/create returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in, so console labels weren't observed.

steps.title: Pick least-privilege granular scopes
steps.detail: Map features to service:action:resource scopes (for example meeting:read:meeting, cloud_recording read scopes) and avoid :admin variants unless the agent truly needs account-wide data. Write a one-line justification per scope for review.

steps.title: Implement OAuth (auth code, optional PKCE)
steps.detail: Redirect to https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize, exchange at https://zoom.us/oauth/token. Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens 90 days and rotate on each refresh, so always store the newest one. Public clients must use S256 (plain is the default if omitted).

steps.title: Install via Local Test and verify
steps.detail: Use the app's Local Test page to add it to your own account, then call GET https://api.zoom.us/v2/users/me.

steps.title: (Optional) Request a beta share for pilot customers
steps.detail: In the Beta Test section select Request to Share. After approval, send the authorization URL to up to 10 accounts (account-level) or 100 users (user-level). Renew every 4 weeks (two extensions).

steps.title: Draft technical design and security documentation
steps.detail: Describe architecture, data flow of Zoom data, storage and retention, encryption, AI/LLM processing, and scope justifications; prepare listing copy and a reviewer test plan.

steps.title: Decide listing visibility
steps.detail: To keep installs gated, enable 'From your landing page' so the Marketplace button becomes 'Visit site to add' and put the authorization URL behind your login.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Submit from the app's console page with listing info, documentation, and test credentials.

steps.title: Functional and compliance review
steps.detail: Reviewers test install, uninstall, configuration, sign-up and data flow; compliance reviews your technical design document.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: SLA from a Zoom staff forum reply.

steps.title: Security review
steps.detail: Technical design review, OAuth scope evaluation and OWASP Top 10 testing. Failures come back as a remediation report; you fix and resubmit.

steps.title: Publish and monitor
steps.detail: Publish once approved. Beta authorization URLs stop working after publishing, so move pilot users to the published URL. Zoom monitors published apps for ongoing compliance.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Beta URLs invalidating on publish comes from Zoom's Authorization URL FAQ as seen in a search snippet.

blockers.symptom: External user gets an error or can't add the app from your authorization URL
blockers.cause: Unpublished apps can't be added outside your account without an approved beta share, or the 4-week URL has expired.
blockers.fix: Request to Share (3–4 business days) or Request Extension; for production, publish via review.

blockers.symptom: New pilot customers can't install once you hit 10 accounts / 100 users
blockers.fix: Email Zoom with a reason to raise the cap, or finish Marketplace review.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The email-to-raise option comes from a search snippet of Zoom docs.

blockers.symptom: Review returned with a remediation report
blockers.cause: Unnecessary scopes, unclear technical design document, or OWASP findings in security testing.
blockers.fix: Drop unneeded scopes, tighten docs, fix findings, resubmit.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 on API calls, especially for customers on Free plans
blockers.cause: Rate limits are per account and shared across all apps installed on it; Free accounts get as little as 1/sec and 1,000/day for heavy APIs.
blockers.fix: Back off, cache, use webhooks instead of polling, and size features by customer plan.

blockers.cause: Zoom rotates refresh tokens on each refresh and they expire after 90 days; an old token was reused or the user went inactive too long.
blockers.fix: Persist the newest refresh token atomically and re-run authorization when it fails.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error string is our assumption.

nuances.text: Access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens last 90 days and a new one comes with every refresh.
Rate limits are shared by all apps installed on an account, so another vendor's integration can eat your customer's quota.
Public clients without a secret always show the consent screen.
A published app can still be gated: 'From your landing page' replaces the Add button with 'Visit site to add' so only your signed-in users reach the authorization URL.
Load testing and DoS simulations aren't part of Zoom's security review, but OWASP Top 10 testing and vulnerable-library checks are.
